Pick a folder once and Forkcast saves an encrypted backup there on the days you choose. It can be on this phone, an SD card, or a cloud app\'s folder (Google Drive, OneDrive and others). Forkcast only sees that folder.
Saving to the folder you chose
Stop automatic backups to this folder?
Backups stop and Forkcast lets go of the folder. Backups already there stay.
Forkcast can\'t reach the backup folder any more. It may have been moved or deleted. Choose a folder again.
Backups are set to use a password, but none is saved on this phone. Turn the password off and on again to set it.
The backup couldn\'t be saved. Check that there\'s free space, or choose another folder.
Deleting backups needs your phone\'s screen lock (PIN, pattern, password, fingerprint or face), so nobody holding your phone can remove them.
Backups from %1$s to %2$s will be deleted from your backup folder. This can\'t be undone.
The backup from %1$s will be deleted from your backup folder. This can\'t be undone.

The newest backup (%1$s) has a password other than the one saved for automatic backups, so it couldn\'t be checked and nothing was deleted. Back up now, then the old ones can go.

Set. Every backup is encrypted with it.
To see or change your backup password
Set a screen lock on this phone first. Forkcast asks for it before showing or changing your backup password.
Save it in your password manager. If you lose this phone, it\'s the only way to open your backups.
Your backups in the backup folder are encrypted again with the new password. Copies saved anywhere else keep the old one.

This file is not encrypted. It includes your API keys and all your health data in readable form: food log, weights, water, activity, goals and profile, settings, AI services and meal photos. Anyone with the file can see and use them.
To save a backup without encryption
Set a screen lock on this phone first. Forkcast asks for it before saving a backup anyone could read.
Every backup holds everything: your log and foods, settings, AI services and their keys, and meal photos.
Backup files are named by date and time, for example %1$s. Copies without encryption end in _unencrypted.

Your meals and daily totals, as a PDF to print or a spreadsheet, to share with a doctor or dietitian.
Each meal with its time, foods, amounts, calories and macros, and each day\'s totals against your targets. No photos.
